input.strategy_title: AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement for serving and training
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Two strategic customers are standardizing on AMD Instinct accelerators and need
RHOAI to serve and train on ROCm. Upstream vLLM and PyTorch both publish ROCm
support, but the platform ships only CUDA runtime builds, and we have no
first-hand data on functional or performance parity for our supported model
set. Feature and performance validation requires physical AMD GPU hardware —
none exists in our CI fleet today — and upstream ROCm image cadence is
controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | A validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the supported model set, producing the go/no-go scope for productization. |
| HLR-2 | P0 | A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is productized for the models the validation campaign clears. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue, with amd.com/gpu quota handling. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, and the validated model list. |

## Affected Components

- KServe
- Serving Runtimes
- Training Operator
- Distributed Workloads

## Out of Scope

- Intel Gaudi or other non-AMD accelerator families
- AMD GPU sharing/partitioning support

## Open Questions

1. Hardware access: the validation campaign (HLR-1) needs dedicated AMD
   Instinct nodes — procurement or partner-lab access is unresolved.
2. Upstream ROCm build cadence: whether AMD's runtime image releases align
   with our release trains is outside our control.

# AMD Instinct validation campaign: vLLM serving functional and performance parity

## Description

This epic delivers the validation campaign on physical AMD Instinct hardware
that establishes functional and performance parity data for vLLM serving of the
platform's supported model set on ROCm, and produces the go/no-go scope for
productization. It is the strategy's decision gate: the productization of a
supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime proceeds for exactly the models this
campaign clears.

## Scope

- Secure access to dedicated AMD Instinct nodes (procurement or partner-lab
  access) and stand up the ROCm system stack on them: ROCm drivers, the AMD GPU
  operator / device plugin stack, and verification that `amd.com/gpu` resources
  are discoverable and consumable by pods.
- Select and record the vLLM ROCm runtime image used for the campaign (upstream
  AMD-published or self-built) and its provenance, including the upstream ROCm
  release it is based on.
- For each model in the supported model set, exercise vLLM serving on ROCm and
  record a pass/fail functional result (correct inference behavior on the
  model's supported task surface).
- For each functionally passing model, record performance measurements
  (throughput and latency) and produce performance parity data relative to the
  platform's CUDA runtime builds.
- Produce the validation report: per-model functional and performance outcomes,
  the ROCm stack and image versions used, and the resulting go/no-go
  recommendation with the cleared model list for productization.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The ROCm system stack (drivers and AMD GPU operator / device plugin) is
  installed on the campaign's AMD Instinct nodes and verified to expose
  `amd.com/gpu` resources that pods can request and use.
- Every model in the supported model set has a recorded functional pass/fail
  result for vLLM serving on ROCm.
- Every functionally passing model has recorded performance measurements with
  parity data relative to the CUDA runtime builds.
- The validation report is delivered, stating per-model outcomes, the exact ROCm
  stack and runtime image versions used, and a go/no-go recommendation with the
  explicit cleared model list.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): fully covered — this epic is the validation campaign and produces
  the go/no-go scope for productization.

## Risks and Notes

- Hardware access (procurement or partner-lab) is an externally controlled
  availability precondition; securing it is part of this epic's work, but the
  access being granted is not an acceptance condition on the deliverable.
- Upstream ROCm image release cadence is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities; the campaign records which images were used so the
  productization decision can account for cadence.

# Productize supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime

## Description

This epic productizes a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime for the models the
AMD Instinct validation campaign clears: a released runtime image, its
ServingRuntime definition for KServe InferenceServices, and the image
sourcing/rebase strategy relative to upstream ROCm release cadence.

## Scope

- Build and release a supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime image for the cleared
  model set, through the existing Serving Runtimes build and release process.
- Provide the ServingRuntime/ClusterServingRuntime definition that exposes the
  ROCm runtime to KServe InferenceServices, requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources
  on AMD GPU nodes.
- Determine and document the runtime's image sourcing and rebase strategy
  (upstream AMD-published ROCm images versus self-built), accounting for the
  upstream ROCm release cadence relative to platform release trains.
- Validate serving through KServe on AMD GPU nodes (KServe component
  validation): the productized runtime deploys under InferenceServices and
  serves predictions for the cleared model set.
- Update any incidental runtime-related references (supported-accelerator
  labels, image references) that fall out of this change.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime image is built and released for the
  current platform version through the Serving Runtimes build pipeline, and the
  pipeline run is green.
- A ServingRuntime definition exposes the ROCm runtime, requesting
  `amd.com/gpu` resources, and is accepted by the KServe CRD surface.
- The productized runtime serves predictions through KServe InferenceServices
  on AMD GPU nodes for every model on the cleared list from the validation
  campaign.
- The image sourcing and rebase strategy is documented and reproducible, stating
  which upstream ROCm releases it tracks and the fallback when upstream cadence
  does not align with a platform release train.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): fully covered — the supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime is
  productized for the models the validation campaign clears.
- Covers the KServe affected-component validation (passive component, same
  team): serving on AMD nodes under KServe is verified here.

## Risks and Notes

- Scope is parameterized by the validation campaign's cleared model list; a
  partial clear narrows the released model set, and a no-go descopes this epic.
- Upstream ROCm image release timing is controlled by AMD and the upstream
  communities and may not align with platform release trains; the documented
  sourcing strategy must state the fallback.

# PyTorch ROCm training support in Training Operator

## Description

This epic delivers PyTorch training support on ROCm for single- and multi-GPU
jobs running as PyTorchJobs through the Training Operator, including admission
through Kueue.

## Scope

- Enable PyTorchJob execution on ROCm-enabled nodes for single-GPU and
  multi-GPU (multi-worker) topologies: validated PyTorch ROCm worker image
  guidance/defaults and any operator changes needed for AMD GPU resource
  handling in job pods.
- Verify that PyTorchJobs requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources run to completion
  on AMD GPU nodes in both single-GPU and multi-GPU topologies.
- Verify that such jobs are queued and admitted through Kueue when workload
  queueing is enabled, exercising the platform's queueing configuration for AMD
  GPU resources.
- Document the supported job specification shape for ROCm training jobs
  (captured as engineering guidance consumed by the documentation epic).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A PyTorchJob requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources on a single GPU runs to
  successful completion on ROCm-enabled nodes.
- A multi-GPU (multi-worker) PyTorchJob requesting `amd.com/gpu` resources runs
  to successful completion on ROCm-enabled nodes.
- The above jobs are admitted through Kueue when queueing is enabled, and the
  admission behavior is recorded as a validation result.
- Any operator changes required for AMD GPU resource handling in PyTorchJob
  pods are implemented and covered by the validation above.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, training portion): PyTorch training on ROCm is supported for
  single- and multi-GPU jobs admitted through Kueue.

## Risks and Notes

- Verification requires access to AMD GPU nodes; this epic can be implemented
  ahead of hardware availability but cannot be validated without it.
- The PyTorch ROCm worker images depend on upstream ROCm releases whose cadence
  is controlled by AMD and the upstream communities.

# Kueue amd.com/gpu quota handling for AMD GPU workloads

## Description

This epic delivers `amd.com/gpu` quota handling in the platform's Kueue-based
queueing layer, so workloads requesting AMD GPU resources are admitted under
the ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model like their NVIDIA counterparts.

## Scope

- Extend the Kueue quota configuration to cover `amd.com/gpu` resources:
  quota flavors and queue configuration for AMD GPU nodes within the existing
  ClusterQueue/LocalQueue model.
- Preserve existing admission semantics for AMD GPU workloads, including
  all-or-nothing (waitForPodsReady) admission and queueing when quota is
  exhausted.
- Verify on AMD GPU nodes that workloads requesting `amd.com/gpu` (for example
  PyTorchJobs) are admitted according to quota and run as admitted.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Kueue quota configuration supports `amd.com/gpu` resources within the
  ClusterQueue/LocalQueue quota model, and the configuration is delivered.
- A workload requesting `amd.com/gpu` is admitted when quota is available and
  queued (not partially admitted) when quota is exhausted.
- Admission of an AMD GPU workload preserves all-or-nothing readiness
  semantics.
- Verification on AMD GPU nodes is recorded: an `amd.com/gpu`-requesting
  workload is admitted under quota and runs to completion.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1, quota portion): `amd.com/gpu` quota handling for jobs admitted
  through Kueue.

## Risks and Notes

- Assumes `amd.com/gpu` resources are exposed on nodes by the AMD GPU
  operator / ROCm device plugin stack, which is not part of the platform
  inventory; the validation campaign covers standing it up on validation nodes.
- Verification requires access to AMD GPU nodes; the configuration work can be
  implemented ahead of hardware availability.

# AMD GPU (ROCm) enablement documentation

## Description

This epic authors the customer-facing documentation for AMD GPU (ROCm)
enablement: supported AMD hardware, driver prerequisites, the validated model
list for vLLM ROCm serving, and usage of PyTorch ROCm training with Kueue
quota.

## Scope

Content outline (authored through the Red Hat docs content process):

- Supported AMD hardware: which AMD Instinct accelerators are supported for
  serving and training.
- Driver and system prerequisites: ROCm driver stack and node requirements
  customers must meet, including the `amd.com/gpu` resource expectation.
- Validated model list: the models cleared by the validation campaign for vLLM
  ROCm serving, as productized.
- Serving usage: deploying the supported vLLM ROCm serving runtime under KServe
  InferenceServices on AMD GPU nodes.
- Training usage: running single- and multi-GPU PyTorchJobs on ROCm, including
  Kueue quota configuration and admission for `amd.com/gpu` workloads.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics state the supported AMD hardware, the driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list, sourced from the validation
  campaign results and the productized runtime's support surface.
- Documentation covers PyTorch ROCm training usage for single- and multi-GPU
  jobs, including Kueue quota handling for `amd.com/gpu`.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implementations by the
  owning engineering teams before publication.
- The topics are published in the product documentation set.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): documentation states supported AMD hardware, driver
  prerequisites, and the validated model list.

## Risks and Notes

- Owning team assumed to be RHOAI Serving (the strategy names no docs owner and
  the Documentation component has no architecture-context file); confirm before
  scheduling.
